blocks.html:
READING PASSAGE 2

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 14–26, which are based on Reading Passage 2 below.

A unique golden textile

A two-man project to use spider silk is achieved after 4 years

Paragraph A

A A rare textile made from the silk of more than a million wild spiders has been on display at the American Museum of Natural History in New York City. To produce this golden cloth, 70 people spent four years collecting golden-orb spiders from telephone poles in Madagascar, while another dozen workers carefully extracted about 80 feet of silk filament from each of the arachnids. The resulting 11-foot-by-4-foot textile is the only large piece of cloth made from natural spider silk in the world today.

Paragraph B

B Spider silk is very elastic and strong compared with steel or Kevlar, said textile expert Simon Peers, who co-led the project. Kevlar is a lightweight synthetic fabric, chemically related to nylon, that is used in bullet-proof vests. Kevlar is resistant to wear, tear and heat and has virtually no melting point. But the tensile strength of spider silk is even greater than Kevlar's aramid filaments and higher than that of high-grade steel. Most importantly, spider silk is extremely lightweight: a strand long enough to circle the Earth would weigh less than 500 grams (18 oz). It is also especially ductile, able to stretch up to 140 percent of its length without breaking and to retain its strength below –40 °C, giving it toughness equal to that of leading commercial fibres.

Paragraph C

C Researchers have long been intrigued by the unique properties of spider silk. Unfortunately, spider silk is extremely hard to mass-produce. Unlike silkworms—easy to raise in captivity—spiders have a habit of biting off each other's heads when housed together. According to Peers, there is intensive research worldwide aimed at replicating spider-silk tensile properties for use in medicine and industry, but no-one has yet reproduced all the qualities of natural silk.

Paragraph D

D Peers conceived the idea of weaving spider silk after reading about French missionary Jacob Paul Camboué, who worked with spiders in Madagascar during the 1880s and 1890s. Camboué built a small hand-driven machine to extract silk from up to 24 spiders at once, without harming them: the spiders were briefly restrained, their silk collected, then released. Peers built a replica of this 24-spider “silking” machine, said co-leader Nicholas Godley. As a test the pair collected about 20 spiders. “When we stuck them in the machine and started turning it, lo and behold, this beautiful gold-coloured silk started coming out,” Godley recalled.

Paragraph E

E To make a textile of any significant size, the scale had to increase dramatically. Fourteen thousand spiders yield about an ounce of silk, Godley said, and the finished textile weighs about 2.6 pounds. By the end, handlers had worked with more than one million female golden-orb spiders—abundant in Madagascar and famed for their golden thread. Because the spiders produce silk only in the rainy season, all were collected between October and June. An additional 12 workers used hand-powered machines to extract the silk and twist it into 96-filament yarn. After “silking”, the spiders were released; within a week they regenerate their silk, allowing the same individuals to be used again—“the gift that never stops giving,” said Godley.

Paragraph F

F Spending four years to produce a single piece of cloth is hardly practical for scientists or companies hoping to exploit spider silk in biomedicine or as a Kevlar alternative. Several groups have inserted spider genes into bacteria and even goats to make silk, but results have been only partly successful. One reason is that spider silk begins as a liquid protein produced in a special gland in the abdomen. Using the spinneret, the spider applies force that rearranges the protein's molecular structure, transforming it into solid fibre. “When we talk about a spider spinning silk, we're talking about how it applies forces to convert liquid to solid,” explained spider-silk expert Todd Blackledge of the University of Akron, who was not involved in the project. “Every year we get closer to mass production, but we're not there yet.” For now, we must be content with one extraordinarily beautiful cloth—courtesy of more than a million spiders.

questionGroups.bodyHtml:
Questions 14–19

Reading Passage 2 has six paragraphs A–F.

Choose the correct heading for each paragraph from the list of headings below.

Drag a heading from the list and drop it onto the correct paragraph's answer box on the left.

List of Headings
i. Experimenting with an old idea
ii. Life cycle of Madagascar spiders
iii. Advances in the textile industry
iv. Resources needed to meet the project's demands
v. The physical properties of spider silk
vi. A scientific analysis of spider silk
vii. A unique work of art
viii. Importance of the silk-textile market
ix. Difficulties of raising spiders in captivity

Questions 20–23

Look at the following statements (Questions 20–23) and the list of researchers below.

Match each statement with the correct researcher, A, B or C.

NB You may use any letter more than once.

20 It takes a tremendous number of spiders to make a small amount of silk.

21 Scientists want to use the qualities of spider silk for medical purposes.

22 Scientists are making some progress in their efforts to manufacture spider silk.

23 Spider silk compares favourably to materials known for their strength.

List of Researchers
A Simon Peers
B Nicholas Godley
C Todd Blackledge

Questions 24–26

Complete the summary below.

Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.

Producing spider silk in the lab

Both scientists and manufacturers are interested in producing silk for many different purposes. Some researchers have tried to grow silk by introducing genetic material into 24 and some animals. But these experiments have been somewhat disappointing.

It is difficult to make spider silk in a lab setting because the silk comes from a liquid protein made in a 25 inside the spider's body. When a spider spins silk, it applies 26 that turns this liquid into solid silk. Scientists cannot replicate this yet.

passageNotes.label: Paragraph A
passageNotes.text: 一件由超 100 万只野生蜘蛛丝制成的稀有纺织品，曾在美国自然历史博物馆展出。这件金色织物的制作耗时四年，70 人在马达加斯加的电线杆上收集金球蜘蛛（golden-orb spiders），另有 12 人从每只蜘蛛身上小心提取约 80 英尺（约 24 米）的丝线。最终制成的 11 英尺 ×4 英尺（约 3.4 米 ×1.2 米）织物，是当今世界唯一一件大型天然蜘蛛丝纺织品。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph B
passageNotes.text: 纺织品专家西蒙・皮尔斯（Simon Peers）（项目联合负责人）表示，蜘蛛丝的弹性和强度远超钢材和凯夫拉（Kevlar，一种轻质合成纤维，与尼龙化学性质相似，用于防弹背心，耐磨、抗撕裂、耐高温且几乎无熔点）。蜘蛛丝的抗拉强度甚至超过凯夫拉的芳纶纤维和高档钢材，且极具轻量化优势 —— 一根足够绕地球一周的蜘蛛丝，重量不足 500 克（18 盎司）。此外，蜘蛛丝延展性极佳，可拉伸至原长的 140% 而不断裂，在 - 40℃以下仍能保持强度，韧性堪比主流商业纤维。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph C
passageNotes.text: 研究人员长期对蜘蛛丝的独特性能感兴趣，但蜘蛛丝极难量产。与易人工饲养的蚕不同，蜘蛛在群居时会相互残杀（咬掉对方头部）。皮尔斯指出，全球有大量研究旨在复制蜘蛛丝的抗拉性能，用于医学和工业领域，但尚未有人能完全复现天然蜘蛛丝的所有特性。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph D
passageNotes.text: 皮尔斯的蜘蛛丝编织想法，源于阅读 19 世纪 80-90 年代法国传教士雅各布・保罗・坎布埃（Jacob Paul Camboué）在马达加斯加研究蜘蛛的记载。坎布埃发明了一种手动机器，可同时从 24 只蜘蛛身上提取丝线且不伤害它们（短暂固定蜘蛛、收集丝线后释放）。项目联合负责人尼古拉斯・戈德利（Nicholas Godley）表示，皮尔斯复制了这种 “24 蜘蛛抽丝机”，两人先以 20 只蜘蛛做测试：“将蜘蛛放入机器转动时，令人惊喜的是，美丽的金色丝线开始产出”。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph E
passageNotes.text: 要制作一定尺寸的纺织品，规模需大幅扩大。戈德利称，1.4 万只蜘蛛仅能产出约 1 盎司（约 28 克）丝线，而成品织物重约 2.6 磅（约 1.2 公斤）。最终，工作人员共处理超 100 万只雌性金球蜘蛛（马达加斯加常见物种，以金色丝线闻名）。因蜘蛛仅在雨季产丝，所有蜘蛛均在 10 月至次年 6 月收集。另有 12 名工人用手动机器提取丝线，捻成 96 缕纱线。抽丝后蜘蛛被释放，一周内即可再生丝线，可重复使用 —— 戈德利称之为 “不竭的馈赠”。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph F
passageNotes.text: 耗时四年制作单件织物，对希望将蜘蛛丝用于生物医学或替代凯夫拉的科学家和企业而言，显然不现实。已有研究团队将蜘蛛基因植入细菌甚至山羊体内尝试产丝，但成果有限。原因之一是，蜘蛛丝最初是蜘蛛腹部特殊腺体分泌的液态蛋白质，蜘蛛通过纺绩器施加力，重组蛋白质分子结构，将其转化为固态纤维。未参与该项目的阿克伦大学蜘蛛丝专家托德・布莱克利奇（Todd Blackledge）解释：“蜘蛛纺丝的核心，是通过施力将液态转化为固态”。“我们每年都在接近量产，但尚未成功”。目前，人们只能满足于这一件异常美丽的织物 —— 由超 100 万只蜘蛛 “贡献” 而成。

questionExplanations.sectionTitle: 1. 段落标题匹配（Questions 14–19：Choose the correct heading）

items.text:
（1）题目 14：Paragraph A
答案：vii（A unique work of art，一件独特的艺术品）
解析：Paragraph A 强调该蜘蛛丝织物 “由超 100 万只蜘蛛制成”“全球唯一大型天然蜘蛛丝纺织品”，核心是 “独特性”，与标题 vii 一致，因此选 vii。

（2）题目 15：Paragraph B
答案：v（The physical properties of spider silk，蜘蛛丝的物理特性）
解析：Paragraph B 详细描述蜘蛛丝的 “强度、轻量化、延展性、低温韧性” 等物理属性，与标题 v 一致，因此选 v。

（3）题目 16：Paragraph C
答案：ix（Difficulties of raising spiders in captivity，人工饲养蜘蛛的困难）
解析：Paragraph C 指出 “蜘蛛群居会相互残杀”，核心是 “人工饲养的困难”，与标题 ix 一致，因此选 ix。

（4）题目 17：Paragraph D
答案：i（Experimenting with an old idea，基于旧想法的实验）
解析：Paragraph D 讲述皮尔斯复制 19 世纪传教士的 “抽丝机” 并进行测试，核心是 “基于旧想法的实验”，与标题 i 一致，因此选 i。

（5）题目 18：Paragraph E
答案：iv（Resources needed to meet the project’s demands，满足项目需求所需的资源）
解析：Paragraph E 说明制作织物需 “超 100 万只蜘蛛、特定季节收集、12 名工人”，核心是 “项目所需资源”，与标题 iv 一致，因此选 iv。

（6）题目 19：Paragraph F
答案：vi（A scientific analysis of spider silk，蜘蛛丝的科学分析）
解析：Paragraph F 分析 “基因工程产丝的局限、蜘蛛纺丝的科学原理”，核心是 “科学分析”，与标题 vi 一致，因此选 vi。

questionExplanations.sectionTitle: 2. 研究者 - 观点匹配（Questions 20–23：Match each statement with the correct researcher）

items.text:
（1）题目 20：It takes a tremendous number of spiders to make a small amount of silk.（制作少量丝线需大量蜘蛛）
答案：B（Nicholas Godley，尼古拉斯・戈德利）
解析：定位 Paragraph E 中 “Fourteen thousand spiders yield about an ounce of silk, Godley said”，明确提到戈德利指出 “1.4 万只蜘蛛产 1 盎司丝线”，与题干一致，因此选 B。

（2）题目 21：Scientists want to use the qualities of spider silk for medical purposes.（科学家希望将蜘蛛丝的特性用于医学目的）
答案：A（Simon Peers，西蒙・皮尔斯）
解析：定位 Paragraph C 中 “According to Peers, there is intensive research worldwide aimed at replicating spider-silk tensile properties for use in medicine and industry”，明确提到皮尔斯指出 “研究旨在将蜘蛛丝特性用于医学”，与题干一致，因此选 A。

（3）题目 22：Scientists are making some progress in their efforts to manufacture spider silk.（科学家在人工制造蜘蛛丝方面取得一定进展）
答案：C（Todd Blackledge，托德・布莱克利奇）
解析：定位 Paragraph F 中 “Todd Blackledge... ‘Every year we get closer to mass production, but we’re not there yet’”，明确提到布莱克利奇认为 “每年都在接近量产”，即有进展，与题干一致，因此选 C。

（4）题目 23：Spider silk compares favourably to materials known for their strength.（蜘蛛丝与以强度著称的材料相比更具优势）
答案：A（Simon Peers，西蒙・皮尔斯）
解析：定位 Paragraph B 中 “Simon Peers... the tensile strength of spider silk is even greater than Kevlar’s aramid filaments and higher than that of high-grade steel”，明确提到皮尔斯指出 “蜘蛛丝强度超过凯夫拉和高档钢材”，与题干一致，因此选 A。

items.text:
（1）题目 24：Some researchers have tried to grow silk by introducing genetic material into \___\___ and some animals.
题目翻译：部分研究者尝试将遗传物质植入_\___\__和部分动物体内，以培育产丝能力。
答案：bacteria（细菌）
解析：定位 Paragraph F 中 “Several groups have inserted spider genes into bacteria and even goats to make silk”，明确提到 “将蜘蛛基因植入细菌和山羊”，因此答案为 “bacteria”。

（2）题目 25：It is difficult to make spider silk in a lab setting because the silk comes from a liquid protein made in a \___\___ inside the spider’s body.
题目翻译：实验室难以制造蜘蛛丝，因为蜘蛛丝源自蜘蛛体内_\___\__产生的液态蛋白质。
答案：gland（腺体）
解析：定位 Paragraph F 中 “spider silk begins as a liquid protein produced in a special gland in the abdomen”，明确提到液态蛋白质由 “腹部特殊腺体” 产生，因此答案为 “gland”。

（3）题目 26：When a spider spins silk, it applies \___\___ that turns this liquid into solid silk.
题目翻译：蜘蛛纺丝时，会施加_\___\__将液态转化为固态丝线。
答案：force（力）
解析：定位 Paragraph F 中 “Using the spinneret, the spider applies force that rearranges the protein’s molecular structure, transforming it into solid fibre”，明确提到蜘蛛通过 “施加力” 实现液态到固态的转化，因此答案为 “force”。
